conventions.convention: Covariant two-tensors are pointwise bilinear forms; smoothness means smooth components in every maximal-atlas chart. Coordinate-tuple evaluations mean coordinate representatives. Four-dimensional coordinate labels are 0,1,2,3; label 0 alone implies no causal character.

The manifold is smooth, Hausdorff, second countable, four-dimensional and without boundary; neither nonemptiness nor connectedness is assumed. Metric signature is (-,+,+,+), with inertia (3,1,0). Smooth tangent-bundle sections inherit Countable Choice.

Null and causal vectors exclude zero. Future direction is defined only for nonzero causal vectors, by g(v,N)<0; past direction uses g(v,N)>0. The time-orientation field N is smooth and everywhere timelike.
Smooth future timelike curves have nonempty open interval domains. With supplied c>0, proper time is the oriented integral of sqrt(-g(γ′,γ′))/c; four-velocity has normalization g(U,U)=-c².
The first lower Christoffel index is the differentiating direction. Curvature is R(X,Y)Z=∇X∇YZ−∇Y∇XZ−∇[X,Y]Z, with R(∂c,∂d)∂b=Rᵃ_bcd∂a and Ric_bd=Σa Rᵃ_bad.

SI conventions assign c units m/s, G_N units m³/(kg s²), Λ units m⁻² and κ=8πG_N/c⁴. Orthonormal stress-energy components have energy-density units; SI energy flux is c times the spatial tensor current, and momentum density is its metric-dual covector divided by c. No numerical constants are asserted.

Stress-energy is smooth and symmetric on a nonempty open matter domain. Positivity, conservation and realization by matter are separate requirements. Distributional and nonsmooth interface sources lie outside this definition.

WEC and SEC quantify over timelike vectors; NEC quantifies over nonzero null vectors. DEC tests future timelike vectors and permits zero output through membership in the closed future cone. SEC uses T−(tr_g T)g/2 in four dimensions.
Spacetime and matter postulates are adopted model assumptions, impose no energy condition automatically, assert no measured constants, and do not deductively establish applicability to nature.

load_bearing.statement: A time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold is a triple (M,g,N): M is a smooth four-manifold without boundary, g is a smooth symmetric nondegenerate covariant two-tensor of pointwise inertia (3,1,0), and N is a smooth everywhere timelike vector field.

For the supplied smooth Lorentzian metric, LC(M,g) has a unique element, constructed by 2g(∇X Y,Z)=K(X,Y,Z). It is torsion-free and metric-compatible, with Γᵃ_bc=gᵃᵈ(∂b gdc+∂c gbd−∂d gbc)/2. The item also defines curvature, Ricci and scalar contractions.
A smooth covariant two-tensor field is a family of bilinear maps A_p:T_pM×T_pM→R whose component functions are C∞ in every chart of the maximal smooth atlas.
For a family of covariant two-tensors smooth in one smooth atlas, A′ab(u)=Σcd (∂xᶜ/∂yᵃ)(u)(∂xᵈ/∂yᵇ)(u)Acd(x(u)); its components are smooth in every maximal-atlas chart.

The nondegenerate metric induces flat_p(v)=g_p(v,·), its inverse sharp_p, and g_p⁻¹(α,β)=g_p(sharp_p α,sharp_p β). The metric trace of symmetric A is the trace of v↦sharp_p(A_p(v,·)), with chart formula gᵃᵇAab.
For a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, inverse-metric components are C∞ in every smooth chart and transform contravariantly by the two Jacobian factors ∂y/∂x.

N_p⊥ is three-dimensional and positive definite; every nonzero causal vector pairs nontrivially with N_p. The future timelike component is {v:g_p(v,v)<0, g_p(v,N_p)<0}, and its closure minus zero is exactly the future-directed causal set.
An affine connection is torsion-free iff Γᵃ_bc=Γᵃ_cb in every smooth chart, and metric-compatible iff ∂a gbc=Σd(Γᵈ_ab gdc+Γᵈ_ac gbd) in every smooth chart.

The item fixes SI dimensions and coordinate readings, including κ=8πG_N/c⁴, orthonormal tensor components in J/m³, q_n=cφ_n and p_n=φ_n-flat/c; it states conventions, not a physical law or a measurement.
The item defines WEC, NEC, DEC and SEC pointwise and proves DEC implies WEC, WEC implies NEC, and SEC implies NEC; none is imposed automatically on the matter model.

concerns.concern: Step 1.2 applies metric compatibility to chart-local coordinate fields, whereas def-gr-metric-selected-connection (a) quantifies over smooth fields on all of M. Localization is valid, but the proof does not explain it. A local bump cutoff extending the three fields near an arbitrary point, or an explicitly local compatibility convention, supplies the missing bridge. The same issue occurs in the uniqueness argument of the connection definition.

The paragraph 'Relation to the matter model' says 'for a model derived from an action, T is the Hilbert stress-energy tensor of that action', without defining the Hilbert tensor or identifying its exact definition. The explicit variational definition is on the later Einstein-and-matter page. This is a terminology/ordering deficiency under the mandatory definition rule; no present proof uses the unnamed construction.

Clause (ii) again says an action model 'defines T as the Hilbert stress-energy tensor of that action' without a definition or an exact supplier pointer. Clause (iii) carefully avoids asserting arbitrary-action conservation, but does not remedy this undefined technical term.

Steps 1.1–1.2 use smoothness and derivatives of sine/cosine, injectivity of cosine on (0,π), and injectivity of the circle parametrization on (0,2π). The listed prerequisites supply the inverse-function theorem and tensor transformation, but no exact trigonometric supplier for these properties. The computation is correct; its prerequisite record is incomplete.

alerts.finding: The theorem assumes an arbitrary smooth symmetric nondegenerate metric, but [L5] states 'The components g^{ab} of the inverse metric are smooth' citing lem-gr-inverse-metric-is-smooth, whose Statement assumes a time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold. Likewise the cited musical and metric-selected definitions are formulated for Lorentzian data. The general-signature theorem is true and its Koszul argument otherwise applies, but this supplier use broadens the cited domain without explanation. Smoothness for the broader domain follows directly from the published matrix-inversion lemma.

[L3] says 'a nonzero vector V is future-directed exactly when g(V,∂t)<0'. The cited def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects defines future direction for nonzero causal vectors. In g=−c²dt²+a²dx², V=∂t+(2c/a)∂1 has g(V,∂t)=−c²<0 but g(V,V)=3c²>0, so the stated unrestricted fact is false. Step 2.1 proves its particular tangent null before using the sign criterion, so the example's calculated conclusion survives the correction.

[L3] says 'a nonzero vector is future-directed exactly when g(V,∂t)<0'. This repeats the unrestricted FLRW sign criterion, while def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects restricts it to causal vectors. At any point V=∂t+(2c/a)∂1 has negative pairing with ∂t and positive squared norm 3c². The fact needs its causal hypothesis; this finding concerns that fact rather than a claim that the illustrative record is measured data.
